summary: A 1939 L-4 cab on a short tower in the Bitterroot National Forest, abandoned for nearly two decades, restored in the early 2000s and now a reservable Forest Service rental.

facts.design: 1931-pattern L-4 lookout cab, 14 by 14 ft, on a short log tower

access.note: Booked on Recreation.gov, open mid-June to mid-September at $30 per night. Drive most of the way, then walk a moderate trail. No electricity or water.

visit.trail_note: Drive to the trailhead on FS 714, then walk a moderate trail of roughly half a mile to three-quarters of a mile. Narrow steps and a catwalk lead to the cab.

facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service, Bitterroot National Forest

events.note: Constructed in 1939 and added to the forest's fixed-point fire detection system that year
One of sixteen lookouts manned on the Bitterroot National Forest in 1967
Slated for removal with seven other inactive lookouts; three of that group were saved and restored
1990 Gird Point wildfire killed most subalpine fir below the lookout; firelookout.com says the fire surrounded the tower
Restoration began in 2003 after nearly two decades abandoned; NHLR dates rehabilitation to 2002

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The NRHP nomination and firelookout.com give 10 ft (3.0 m). The Forest Service page and the NHLR give 8 ft. The record's 3.0 m follows the 10-ft figure; the story reports the disagreement.
The NHLR says the cab was rehabilitated in 2002. The NRHP nomination says restoration began in 2003. The story reports both.
The NHLR gives 2,315 m (7,595 ft), which matches the record. The Forest Service page and the nomination give 7,702 ft (about 2,348 m). The story uses 7,702 ft.
The Forest Service page says 11 miles east, firelookout.com says 12 miles ESE, and Recreation.gov says 20 miles east. The story says about 11 miles and attributes it to the Forest Service.
The same Forest Service page gives a half-mile hike in one place and about three-quarters of a mile in another.

notes_for_editor: Construction, design and CCC attribution rest on the NRHP nomination (stated as belief). The brief lists NRHP 100002297 as a register; the nomination file calls the lookout eligible for listing. I did not confirm a listing date or final status, so the story says eligible. The last staffing year is not exact (firelookout.com says into the 1980s; NHLR calls it inactive in 1984). The rental is current per the Forest Service page (undated). Brief record fields (1939 build, L-4 design, 2003 registration) are supported, so no corrections proposed.
